meta.subtitle: Samsung 64 GB DDR5-5600 RDIMM screening on Tyrone MDA200A2N-224 (172.16.11.132) - complete module register with status
meta.platform: Tyrone MDA200A2N-224 / 2x AMD EPYC 9135 (32C/64T, Zen 5 Turin)

executive_summary: Consolidated acceptance record for one day of memory validation on server 172.16.11.132 (Tyrone MDA200A2N-224, dual AMD EPYC 9135, 24 DDR5 slots). 100 Samsung M321R8GA0PB0-CWMCJ 64 GB DDR5-5600 RDIMMs were handled in total. Identical protocol in every campaign: 5-minute 100% memory burn (stress-ng --vm-method all --verify at 91-92% RAM residency), DRAM-bound bandwidth benchmarks (stress-ng stream 256M working set, sysbench 1 GiB private blocks, mbw, NUMA local/remote) and pre/post health diff (AMD EDAC, MCE, BMC SEL, ACPI BERT, dmidecode serial maps). Cumulative: 8.97 billion verified operations over 30.6 minutes of full-pressure burn - zero verification failures, zero ECC errors, zero machine-checks across all campaigns. The platform itself is fully validated: every one of the 24 slots trained good modules during the day, and the CPUs held full ~4.34 GHz boost in every run.

RESULT - see the Complete Module Register: 90 modules are WORKING - OK (each passed at least one 100% verify-burn at full 5600 MT/s in this server) and 10 modules are FAULTY / DAMAGED - REQUIRE RMA (physically label-recorded and quarantined; two of them were firmware-mapped-out in this server with fatal ACPI BERT 'DRAM storage error' records, and one - s/n ...4642E03CB7 - passed an earlier screen before being damaged, so it must NOT be reinstalled). Performance rule established for the fleet: symmetric channel populations scale linearly (24ch 567-581 GB/s; 20ch 484 GB/s = 102% of linear), asymmetric populations are degraded and unstable (314-425 GB/s, 55-75% of baseline). Current server state: interim 22/24 (1.385 TB); closure = install confirmed-good spare ...EEF450 plus one more verified-good module into P0 CH-G / P1 CH-I and run a final 20-minute re-screen (expected ~570-580 GB/s, 1.5 TB). Watch item: TEMP_P0_DIMM_J logged two brief self-clearing upper-critical excursions during write-heavy phases of asymmetric runs.

Module data from SPD; for the 10 quarantined modules the data comes from the physical label (label Mfg code shown in the Part Number column). WORKING - OK = passed at least one 5-minute 100% verify-burn at full 5600 MT/s with zero ECC/verify errors. FAULTY / DAMAGED - RMA = label-recorded faulty or damaged, physically quarantined.

sel_status: Across the day the BMC SEL grew 279 -> 402. Under test: zero new entries in Runs 1-4; +2 in each Run-5 phase (TEMP_P0_DIMM_J 'Upper Critical going high' assert/deassert, 15 s and 9 s, both self-clearing, fans nominal at 14.4 kRPM). Between campaigns: benign PSU AC-loss / chassis-intrusion artifacts from physical work, and 'Memory Device Disabled' (one per affected socket) on every boot that carried a faulty module; ZERO memory events on all clean boots.
dmesg_status: ACPI BERT (AMD firmware-first) identified every bad module at POST: fatal 'Storage error in DRAM memory (0x0000000000040400) ... error_type 15, physical memory map-out event' records at P0MC0 + P1ML0 and later P0MG0 + P1MI0 - four different slots, identical signature, proving module-internal faults (the affected modules are in the register, status FAULTY). BERT was EMPTY on every clean boot. Kernel-side: 0 machine-check events in all six campaigns; AMD EDAC CE=0/UE=0 before and after every burn; no OOM, swap untouched throughout.
findings: MODULE REGISTER (the deliverable): of 100 modules handled, 90 are WORKING - OK (each passed at least one 5-minute 100% verify-burn at full 5600 MT/s with zero ECC/verify errors) and 10 are FAULTY / DAMAGED - REQUIRE RMA (label-recorded, quarantined). Only one of the ten (s/n ...4642E03CB7, register #93) was ever electronically readable in this server - it passed an early screen and was later damaged; it must NOT be reinstalled. The other nine were never SPD-readable here, consistent with dead/failed-training modules (the firmware-mapped-out pairs are among them) or handling damage.

PLATFORM CLEARED: across six campaigns the server showed no fault - all 24 slots trained good modules during the day (no slot/socket damage), CPUs sustained 4339-4346 MHz peak boost in every burn, PSUs and all six fans nominal, and BMC/BERT instrumentation correctly flagged every bad module at POST.

STRESS RECORD: six 5-minute 100% burns totalling 8,965,251,306 verified operations and 30.6 minutes at 91-92% RAM residency - zero verification failures, zero ECC corrected/uncorrected errors, zero machine-checks, zero OOM/swap events. Every module that trained also passed its burn.

POPULATION-GEOMETRY LAW: symmetric populations scale linearly (24 channels: 567.5-581.1 GB/s; symmetric 20 channels: 483.7 GB/s = 102% of linear), asymmetric populations are degraded AND non-deterministic (22 channels: 314.2-425.0 GB/s = 55-75% of baseline, varying boot-to-boot). Single-thread memcpy and NUMA-remote ratio stayed flat throughout - the penalty is pure interleave geometry. Fleet rule: reduced populations MUST be socket-symmetric.
GOOD-SPARE STATUS: s/n 80CE04254742EEF450 (register #45) is the confirmed good spare for this server's two vacant slots; one additional verified-good module is required to restore 24/24.

THERMAL WATCH: TEMP_P0_DIMM_J (module s/n ...E04546, register #42) logged two brief self-clearing upper-critical excursions during write-heavy phases of asymmetric runs (15 s, 9 s); post-test readings normal, fans nominal. Verify during the final symmetric re-screen; if it recurs, swap the module's position to test whether the hot-spot follows it.

METHODOLOGY (pinned): this stress-ng build splits --vm-bytes across workers (size as TOTAL with --vm-keep); stress-ng --stream on EPYC needs --stream-l3-size 256M (default cache-detection inflates 2.4x); sysbench memory needs 1 GiB private blocks, scope=local (defaults measure cache on reads and lock contention on writes).
recommendations: RMA package: submit the ten FAULTY/DAMAGED modules (register rows 91-100, with label serials and mfg codes) together with this consolidated report and the five per-run reports as evidence. Keep the quarantine physically segregated and marked.

Closure for 172.16.11.132: install good spare s/n 80CE04254742EEF450 (register #45) plus ONE additional verified-good 64 GB module into P0 CH-G and P1 CH-I (restoring symmetric 12+12, 1.5 TB) and run the standard 20-minute re-screen - expected ~570-580 GB/s. Do NOT use ...E03CB7 (register #93).
Until closure, treat the current 22/24 asymmetric configuration as interim: do not deploy bandwidth-sensitive production workloads (55-75% of baseline, non-deterministic across reboots).
Fleet population rule (validated): any reduced DIMM population must keep both sockets symmetric on the same channel letters.
Process SOP (now in effect): record label serials and physically quarantine failed DIMMs at the moment of removal - mapped-out modules expose no SPD.
During the closure re-screen watch TEMP_P0_DIMM_J; afterwards install rasdaemon and enable BIOS patrol scrub, and schedule the 3-hour qualification tier before customer handover.

reproducibility.protocol: Per campaign: dmidecode -t 17 serial map + EDAC/MCE/SEL/BERT baseline -> 5-min stress-ng --vm 64 --vm-bytes <92% MemAvailable, total> --vm-keep --vm-method all --verify burn with 20 s sampler -> stress-ng --stream 64 --stream-l3-size 256M -> sysbench memory 1 GiB blocks/thread scope=local read+write 64T -> mbw 1T -> numactl-bound mbw local/remote -> EDAC/MCE/SEL/BERT/temperature diff
reproducibility.evidence: ACPI BERT fatal records (P0MC0, P1ML0, P0MG0, P1MI0); BMC SEL 'Memory Device Disabled' entries on every faulty-module boot; dmidecode SPD enumeration per run; physical label data for the 10 quarantined modules (register rows 91-100)
reproducibility.tooling_gotchas: stress-ng --vm-bytes = TOTAL split across workers on this build; --stream needs --stream-l3-size 256M on EPYC; sysbench memory needs --memory-block-size=1G --memory-scope=local
